newsitem.title: BELGIUM: INSIGHT - Slowing momentum caps Bel-20 -chartists.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Slowing momentum caps Bel-20 -chartists.

text.p: Belgian analysts turned more cautious on the Bel-20 share index, foreseeing little upside scope in the near term as momentum slowed.
A steady dollar and relatively low interest rates should, however, mean support at 1,800 points will hold.

CERA - The Bel-20 index will be driven by earnings, Wall Street and a stronger dollar and less by interest rates. A stronger dollar helps Belgian exporters as it makes their goods more competitive abroad and means they receive more francs for their U.S. earnings. We expect earnings of Belgian companies to be up 12 percent. In our opinion the dollar will trade at 1.56 marks (32.15 bfr) in three months and 1.57 marks (32.30 bfr) in one year. The Dow Jones will trade at the same levels in 12 months. As a result we expect the economy to continue to grow without fuelling inflation. -- Guy Sips.

BANK DEGROOF - The market will be stuck in the 1,830 - 1,780 range to a lack of events. No figures are due before Wednesday (U.S. GDP) and Friday, but anyway Belgium will be closed (on Friday). So even if there is slight upside pressure on the 10-year yield the index will be strongly supported at 1,780 where we would buy if ever approached (one can dream). Dollar nervousness could bring some volatility (like last week) on dollar-sensitive stocks (see Delhaize, Bekaert). -- Joel Crevecoeur.

ECOFIS - The doji star in the weekly chart may mean at least a pause. The daily chart formed a top below the previous all-time top of Oct 3 at 1,830. As long as the Bel-20 does not fall below 1,759, i.e. the last local low reached in the week Oct 7-11, the long-term uptrend remains in tact. -- Frank Boll.

GENERALE BANK - The Bel-20 broke through resistance levels, but tried in vain in to get close to the year high at 1,830. As long as we stay above 1,800, some upward potential remains. Momentum is slowing and the short-term is turning neutral. Trading tools like stochastics are already giving first indications of a reversing trend, though this weakness needs confirmation. The 1,800 level is important, but even more so the 1,780 level as it is confirmed by different approaches. Some sideways trading is likely in coming days. -- Geert Vanderbeke.

PARIBAS BANK - The closing of the Bel-20 above the previous week's close will probably continue to underpin Bel-20 this week. Strong support at 1,790 and 1,800 holds the key for tests of new highs at 1,850, while a break would start a correction towards the Oct 10 low of 1,760. As long as dollar/mark remains above 1.5000, as long as term rates remain near six percent, we do not believe in a crash scenario in the very near future, but nevertheless we are holding our stop-loss levels just below 1,760. -- Philip Tortelboom.
